extracted.intended_audience: Congressional staff and patent stakeholders (USPTO examiners, practitioners, policymakers)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and evaluative criteria used by the USPTO to measure and improve the quality, clarity, and reliability of patent examination and issued patents across technologies, and to manage examiner performance and resources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consistent application of 35 U.S.C. § 112(a)
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 112 applies to all industries and inventions; USPTO trains examiners to apply Section 112 to all industries and does not instruct examiners to apply §112(a) more rigorously for some industries than others.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: There is more judicial precedent applying §112(a) in life sciences than computer technologies; to ensure consistency USPTO delivered targeted §112 training in FY2019 in areas perceived as treated less rigorously and is exploring additional guidance and training to raise examiner awareness on proper application of §112(a). The USPTO also issued January 2019 guidance addressing written description and enablement issues under §112(a), especially for computer-implemented functional claims that recite only a solution or outcome without reciting how the solution is accomplished. The USPTO will monitor effects of guidance and consider additional guidance if needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allocation of examination time tailored to application attributes
rubrics_metrics.description: Examination time is adjusted and should be tailored to specific attributes of an application so examiners have adequate time to apply patent statutes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Since October 2019, examiners receive additional time based on attributes including overall number of claims, length of the specification, and number of pages in any filed information disclosure statements; examiners with least time also received increases. USPTO plans further time increases and an updated automatic assignment process (classification 'picture' and examiner workload/experience) to match applications to the examiner best suited to examine them. USPTO will continue to monitor examining time to ensure appropriateness and that pendency goals are met.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rigorous application of Sections 102 and 103 (novelty/obviousness)
rubrics_metrics.description: Examiners should properly interpret claim scope, perform high-quality prior art searches, evaluate and analyze relevant prior art, apply it to claims when appropriate, and clearly convey patentability determinations in office actions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: USPTO provides training on claim interpretation; principles of §§112, 102, 103; legal argument analysis; proper prior art searching techniques; and discipline-specific databases including non-patent literature. Additional initiatives include more examination time, improved workload assignments, enhanced prior-art resources, and more comprehensive patent quality reviews.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pendency and transparency metrics (first action and final disposition)
rubrics_metrics.description: Publish pendency statistics that inform stakeholders about timeliness of examination, including first action pendency and average months until final disposition (issuance or abandonment).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: USPTO publishes pendency data on the Patents Dashboard and plans to increase focus on compliance rates with patent term adjustment statutes as measures that provide greater transparency and certainty than simple average pendency measures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Representative sampling of office actions for quality review
rubrics_metrics.description: OPQA's random sample of office actions is intended to be representative of the entire examining corps to detect quality issues and patterns.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Random sampling can be supplemented with targeted reviews when indications suggest deeper review would be beneficial. The majority of individual-examiner review data comes from supervisory patent examiners (SPEs) conducting routine reviews and using the same review form as OPQA to create richer data for trend analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of process metrics to identify quality outliers
rubrics_metrics.description: Use process-type metrics (e.g., allowance rates, appeal rates) in Quality Index Reports to spot individual examiners with behaviors outside norms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: SPEs and managers compare these metrics to art unit or technology center averages to identify potential issues, then investigate whether the behavior reflects best practices or needs assistance, and coach examiners accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review of later office actions that introduce new grounds of rejection
rubrics_metrics.description: Compare second and later office actions that contain new rejections based on new prior art references (without applicant amendments) to identify cases where first-action prior-art search quality may have been poor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: SPEs already review later office actions as part of supervisory duties; current IT systems do not support automated targeted identification of such office actions, but USPTO is refining big-data capabilities to enable this in the future.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prior art search quality assessment and feedback
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess and improve the quality of examiners' recorded prior art searches and search strategies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OPQA completed a pilot where reviewers used a more robust search form, performed separate searches, compared results with the examiner's search, and met with the examiner to discuss findings. Reviewers and examiners found the form and discussions helpful for improving prior art searches; USPTO is expanding search feedback efforts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stakeholder perception measurement
rubrics_metrics.description: Measure customer perceptions of patent quality using surveys and other feedback mechanisms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: USPTO conducts a semi-annual survey of frequent filers (those with six or more patent applications in prosecution) to monitor perception changes; it also uses random surveys of website visitors and other touchpoints and monitors feedback from contact centers and programs like the Patents Ombudsman to capture broader stakeholder views.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarity of office actions
rubrics_metrics.description: Office actions should be clear in articulating statutory rejections, meanings of claim terms or claim scope, and reasons for allowances so rejections are understandable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: USPTO updated its office action review form to measure multiple components of clarity and will use the updated form to capture not only non-compliance but also specific reasons (correctness or clarity concerns). The new performance appraisal plan provides a roadmap emphasizing clarity; OPQA reviewers now also provide positive recognition for best practices in correctness and clarity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Performance Appraisal Plan (PAP) emphasizing search, compact prosecution, and clarity
rubrics_metrics.description: Examiners' performance ratings will be partly based on exemplary practices that demonstrate comprehensive searching, compact prosecution, and clarity in the written record.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exemplary activities for comprehensive search include: searching the inventive concept as defined at the time of first action on the merits; citing prior art pertinent to significant though unclaimed features or the state of the art; and providing brief descriptions in office actions for relevant prior art cited but not applied. For compact prosecution and clarity, exemplary activities include providing annotations showing where claim limitations are met by prior art, providing proper reasons for allowance, and suggesting ways for applicants to overcome rejections. The new PAP was planned for implementation in FY2021 and includes more detail (pages 7–8 of PAP).

rubrics_metrics.name: Funding stability (end fee diversion) to support quality improvements
rubrics_metrics.description: Allowing the USPTO access to collected fees (ending fee diversion) provides funding certainty that enables long-term investments in personnel, technology, and processes that improve patent quality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: USPTO and stakeholder advisory bodies consistently assert that fee stability improves ability to plan and implement training, automated docketing, updated IT systems, and other quality-enhancing investments; proposals (S.2082/H.R.3666) for a revolving fund would facilitate continued investment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deployment of new technologies for improved prior art search
rubrics_metrics.description: Develop and pilot artificial intelligence and machine-learning tools and improved search platforms to assist examiners in locating relevant prior art, including foreign patent documents and non-patent literature.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: USPTO is exploring AI that can learn the language of patent applications across technical disciplines and is pilot testing a new search tool to provide better prior art searching of foreign documents and facilitate future AI/NPL enhancements; development will take significant time and effort.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of a high-quality patent
rubrics_metrics.description: A quality patent is one that was correctly issued in compliance with all requirements of Title 35 and relevant case law at the time of issuance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Invalidation in PTAB or district court does not always indicate poor issuance quality because of legal changes after issuance, close-call decisions, selection bias in challenges (litigation is expensive and selective), and potential prior art not reasonably accessible to examiners. USPTO provides statistics to contextualize challenge rates (e.g., small fraction of patents challenged, outcomes of AIA petitions).

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner oversight, review frequency, and mentoring
rubrics_metrics.description: Balance examiner autonomy (primary examiners authorized to sign documents) with periodic supervisory reviews, OPQA random reviews, and performance monitoring to ensure consistent, reliable work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Primary examiner status requires significant experience and rigorous testing; SPEs perform periodic reviews and statistical comparisons (allowance rates, RCEs, etc.) to identify outliers; pilot programs pair OPQA reviewers with individual examiners for one-on-one prior art search feedback and training; USPTO is exploring additional OPQA–examiner partnership programs to improve skills.

rubrics_metrics.name: Measurement and incentive structure to emphasize thorough first action and compact prosecution
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluation systems (count credits and workflow) should incentivize thorough and complete first action on the merits and compact prosecution to improve overall examination quality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: USPTO restructured distribution of count credit to assign most credit at first action and less for follow-on actions to incentivize complete first-action searches, compact prosecution, and thorough initial office actions. USPTO periodically reviews workflow and quality requirements to balance quality and pendency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent Quality Team activities and examiner training programs
rubrics_metrics.description: Dedicated quality teams and programs should drive continuous improvement through training, assessment, and recognition of best practices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Patent Quality Team has engaged in examiner training (entry-level and refresher), guidance on subject-matter eligibility, restriction practice, interviews, §112 and claim interpretation, examiner trainer development, NPL search training, peer search collaboration pilot, Patent Examiner Technical Training Program (PETTP), Site Experience Education (SEE), STEPP, virtual instructor-led trainings (VILT), patent quality chats, semi-annual Patent Quality Surveys, a customer experience team, updating the master review form (MRF), an accolades program, PTAB Case Study on AIA trials, and the OPQA search feedback pilot. USPTO will continue integrating Office of Patent Quality work with the broader Patents organization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of Global Dossier and international work-sharing to improve efficiency and examination quality
rubrics_metrics.description: Leverage file histories and search/results from other major IP offices to create a more complete patent record and improve examination quality and efficiency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Global Dossier provides single-point access to related applications across IP5 offices; Patent Prosecution Highway (PPH) enables fast-track examination where claims are allowed by another office; Collaborative Search Pilot (CSP) provides multi-office search results early in examination; PCT Collaborative Search & Examination (PCT CS&E) allows IP5 collaboration to produce an ISR and written opinion with contributions from participating offices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Encourage and use third-party pre-issuance submissions
rubrics_metrics.description: Third-party submissions under §122(e) can provide useful prior art and information to examiners when filed in pending applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Since 2012 about 1,000 proper pre-issuance submissions per year have provided over 17,000 documents; most examiners who used such submissions found them helpful. The program has had limited participation and USPTO supports encouraging more robust participation and working with Congress on ways to increase use.

rubrics_metrics.name: Burden allocation and examiner assistance in AIA motions to amend
rubrics_metrics.description: Rulemaking to allocate burdens of persuasion on motions to amend in AIA trials, with the Board evaluating statutory/regulatory requirements and whether petitioners have shown unpatentability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: USPTO issued an NPRM allocating burdens to petitioners based on Federal Circuit decisions and public comments; Board may exercise discretion to reach determinations when appropriate. Under pilot programs, if a petitioner ceases participation, the Board may solicit examiner assistance to prepare advisory reports addressing patentability of proposed substitute claims based on prior art provided or found by the examiner.

rubrics_metrics.name: Incentivizing humanitarian-use innovations (Patents for Humanity certificate transferability)
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide incentives for use of inventions for humanitarian needs via awards and acceleration certificates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: USPTO believes making Patents for Humanity Acceleration Certificates transferable would provide further incentives for inventions that deliver affordable, scalable, sustainable humanitarian solutions.
